title: Proving Circuit Functional Equivalence in Zero Knowledge
excerpt: ZK-CEC combines formal verification and zero-knowledge proofs to verify that a private circuit matches a public specification. It enables verification of third-party hardware designs without revealing their proprietary implementation.
citation: Sirui Shen, Zunchen Huang, Chenglu Jin. (2026). "Proving Circuit Functional Equivalence in Zero Knowledge." arXiv preprint arXiv:2601.11173.

title: Ransomware Negotiation: Dynamics and Privacy-Preserving Mechanism Design
venue: International Conference on Game Theory and AI for Security
excerpt: A finite-horizon bargaining model analyzes negotiations between ransomware attackers and victims. A privacy-preserving mechanism uses secure two-party computation to help both parties agree on a ransom without revealing their private valuations.
citation: Haohui Zhang, Sirui Shen, Xinyu Hu, Chenglu Jin. (2025). "Ransomware Negotiation: Dynamics and Privacy-Preserving Mechanism Design." International Conference on Game Theory and AI for Security, pp. 235-255.

title: Reading it like an open book: Single-trace blind side-channel attacks on garbled circuit frameworks
excerpt: A single-trace blind side-channel attack targets popular garbled circuit frameworks. Secret-dependent AES execution during garbling exposes private inputs without requiring access to protocol plaintexts or ciphertexts.
citation: Sirui Shen, Chenglu Jin. (2024). "Reading it like an open book: Single-trace blind side-channel attacks on garbled circuit frameworks." 2024 Annual Computer Security Applications Conference (ACSAC), pp. 410-424.

title: Heterogeneous reconfigurable accelerator for homomorphic evaluation on encrypted data
excerpt: A heterogeneous reconfigurable accelerator speeds up homomorphic evaluation for the BFV encryption scheme. Modular computing units support number theoretic transforms, residue number system conversion, and other operations on encrypted data.
citation: Wenqing Song, Sirui Shen, Congwei Xu, Yilin Wang, Xinyu Wang, Yuxiang Fu, Li Li, Zhonghai Lu. (2024). "Heterogeneous reconfigurable accelerator for homomorphic evaluation on encrypted data." IEEE Access, 12, pp. 11850-11864.

title: A DSP-purposed reconfigurable acceleration machine (DREAM) for high energy efficiency MIMO signal processing
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I: Regular Papers
excerpt: DREAM is a reconfigurable accelerator for wireless MIMO baseband signal processing. Shared operators, a two-step configuration process, and conflict-free data transfers balance flexibility and energy efficiency.
citation: Yuxiang Fu, Kai Chen, Wenqing Song, Guoqiang He, Sirui Shen, Huizheng Wang, Chuan Zhang, Li Li. (2022). "A DSP-purposed reconfigurable acceleration machine (DREAM) for high energy efficiency MIMO signal processing." IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I: Regular Papers, 70(2), pp. 952-965.

title: A hierarchical parallel discrete gaussian sampler for lattice-based cryptography
venue: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
excerpt: A hierarchical parallel discrete Gaussian sampler accelerates sampling for lattice-based cryptography. A three-stage generation strategy reduces the area cost of repeated lookup tables while preserving the required sampling distribution.
citation: Sirui Shen, Wenqing Song, Xinyu Wang, Xinyu Shao, Yuxiang Fu, Zhonghai Lu, Li Li. (2022). "A hierarchical parallel discrete gaussian sampler for lattice-based cryptography." 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS), pp. 1729-1733.

title: A 67.5 μJ/prediction accelerator for spiking neural networks in image segmentation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems II: Express Briefs
excerpt: An energy-efficient accelerator for spiking neural networks uses a reconfigurable neuron processing unit and event-driven dataflow to exploit sparse spikes for image segmentation.
citation: Qinyu Chen, Guoqiang He, Xinyuan Wang, Jin Xu, Sirui Shen, Hui Chen, Yuxiang Fu, Li Li. (2021). "A 67.5 μJ/prediction accelerator for spiking neural networks in image segmentation." IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems II: Express Briefs, 69(2), pp. 574-578.
